# CIA Intends to Release Records on Cold War Spymaster

## Bibliographic identity and selected witness

National Archives, Nazi War Crimes Interagency Working Group announcement, College Park, Maryland,5October2000. The page’s later review date15August2016 is website maintenance metadata, not the announcement date. The saved HTML and extraction preserve the institutional notice read in the prior law packet.

## Reading scope and consumption

Complete6-paragraph institutional announcement dated5October2000, with title/date/contact context; not the released intelligence archive or personnel files. Full named scope was read in the T21 law development; the text hash matches the later T22 consumer-source receipt. This admission reuses that reading and rechecks the exact passages, not a new whole-book or archival investigation. No direct quotation is admitted.

The [language–law–nation history](../../../../histories/places-and-peoples/language-law-nation-centralisation/DEVELOPMENT.md#branch-xi-postwar) consumes the bounded witness in its existing situated branch. Historical claim, legal prescription, authorial comparison and implementation evidence retain separate standing.

## Admitted passages

<a id="nara-2000-gehlen-disclosure-q001"></a>
## Passage card — `nara-2000-gehlen-disclosure-q001` — Acknowledgement and intended release
^nara-2000-gehlen-disclosure-q001

> **Paraphrase (not a quotation):** The notice reports a CIA affidavit acknowledging an intelligence relationship with Reinhard Gehlen, possession of related records and a commitment to process them for release under the Nazi War Crimes Disclosure Act. The IWG coordinates release and public notification. A commitment to process records is not a claim that this admission has read the archive.

- **Locator:** Announcement5October2000, opening paragraph and closing Holtzman/IWG paragraph.
- **Status:** paraphrase-only.
- **Source relation:** Paraphrased.
- **Verification:** exact named scope read in the prior law packet; saved witness and extraction hashes rebound2026-09-08.
- **Provenance:** institutional witness and immutable local-copy hashes above.
- **Use boundary:** Complete6-paragraph institutional announcement dated5October2000, with title/date/contact context; not the released intelligence archive or personnel files.
- **Consumer:** [owning historical branch](../../../../histories/places-and-peoples/language-law-nation-centralisation/DEVELOPMENT.md#branch-xi-postwar).

<a id="nara-2000-gehlen-disclosure-q002"></a>
## Passage card — `nara-2000-gehlen-disclosure-q002` — Postwar institutional relationship
^nara-2000-gehlen-disclosure-q002

> **Paraphrase (not a quotation):** The notice describes Gehlen’s former wartime intelligence role and a postwar network with Nazi and collaborationist backgrounds. It distinguishes the initial Army Intelligence relationship from subsequent CIA responsibility continuing until1956, and identifies the IWG’s postwar-use remit. The notice is an institutional disclosure witness; it does not establish each individual’s conduct, screening history or appointment compliance.

- **Locator:** Announcement5October2000, third through fifth body paragraphs.
- **Status:** paraphrase-only.
- **Source relation:** Paraphrased.
